purpose: Display per-entry archive metadata without granting extraction or verification authority.
presence: An unavailable or unidentified value is empty. A declared zero CRC is displayed as zero. ZIP AE-2 and keyed RAR checks do not expose their stored value as a plaintext CRC.
crc: CRC-16 and CRC-32 are displayed as four or eight uppercase hexadecimal digits. These are declared values, not evidence that content was read or verified.
attributes: Known attributes use directory/archive, system, hidden and read-only positions, with underscores for absent positions: ____, D___, A__R. When directory and archive flags are both present, D precedes A so both remain visible. POSIX modes contribute directory and read-only status only. These display values never authorize filesystem permissions or object creation.
comments: ZIP entry comments use declared UTF-8, a CRC-bound Unicode Comment extra, or the resolved legacy name encoding with CP437 fallback. ARJ entry comments use the resolved name encoding. EGG comments are read lazily from a validated entry subheader range; encrypted comments are unavailable, and legacy bytes are escaped rather than guessed. RAR 1.x inline, RAR 1.5–2.x nested and RAR 3/4 child CMT comments are decoded on request by the isolated worker; archive-level comments are not file comments. Recognized UTF-16 CMT flags are respected, and other old text uses the resolved name encoding with CP437 fallback. Damaged, unsupported, or unadmitted comments are empty and never determine payload integrity. Controls and bidirectional formatting controls are replaced in the plain-text view.
bounds: ZIP entry comments are limited by the format's 16-bit field and existing directory-read budget. EGG comment display captures at most 65,535 bytes and 1 MiB of subheader work per entry, marking truncation with an ellipsis. RAR comment requests cover at most 128 physical entries per worker, with at most 65,535 UTF-8 bytes per returned comment, 1 MiB of packed CMT data per entry, 32 MiB of cumulative decode work per entry and a separate 64 MiB comment-source read budget. Extended-time CMT comments are decoded without interpreting unrelated timestamps. For salted encryption, candidate salt/time boundaries must fit the complete extended-time suffix; return a comment only when exactly one distinct salt yields its declared CRC. All candidates share the work and password-derivation budgets; ambiguity, exhaustion or failed verification leaves the comment empty. CRC is not cryptographic authentication. Query pages carry at most 1 MiB of raw comments; disk index records, native worker frames and both mailboxes remain bounded and account for added metadata.
unavailable: Formats and record profiles whose parser does not supply a particular property leave that value empty. Implicit directories never inherit a physical record's metadata.
